Retrieve species occurrences from GBIF

Source: R/data_gbif.R
get_gbif_data.Rd

This function retrieves the occurrence records of a species from the Global Biodiversity Information Facility (GBIF), with the public occurrence search API. No account and no API key are needed.

Only records with coordinates and without known geospatial issue are returned.

Usage

get_gbif_data(species, roi = NULL, limit = 1000, ..., api_url = NULL)

Arguments

species

Character. Scientific name of the species, for instance "Apodemus sylvaticus". Underscores are read as spaces, so the names of ocsge_species_dict and eunis_species_dict can be used directly.

roi

An sf (or sfc) object defining the Region Of Interest, in any projection. The search is made on its bounding box, then only the records inside roi are kept. With NULL (default), the search is made on the whole world.

limit

Integer. Maximum number of records to download. Default is 1000. The API does not return more than 100,000 records for one search (see Details).

...

Other filters of the GBIF occurrence search API, as named arguments. For instance year = "2000,2024", coordinateUncertaintyInMeters = "0,100", basisOfRecord = "HUMAN_OBSERVATION" or country = "FR". A range is written "min,max".

api_url

Character. Base URL of the GBIF API. Exposed mainly for testing against a different endpoint.

Value

An sf object of points in EPSG:4326, one row for each record, with the columns:

key

GBIF identifier of the record (https://www.gbif.org/occurrence/<key>).

species

Scientific name of the species.

coordinateUncertaintyInMeters

Uncertainty of the position, in meters. Often NA.

eventDate, year

Date and year of the observation.

basisOfRecord

Type of record, for instance "HUMAN_OBSERVATION" or "PRESERVED_SPECIMEN".

datasetKey

GBIF identifier of the dataset (https://www.gbif.org/dataset/<datasetKey>).

license

License of the record.

The total number of records matching the search in GBIF is stored in the attribute "gbif_count".

Details

The name is first matched against the GBIF taxonomy (species/match), then the records are downloaded by pages of 300 (occurrence/search).

Limitations:

  • The search API stops at 100,000 records. For a larger request, split the region of interest, or the years with year.

  • The search API gives no DOI. For a publication, GBIF asks to cite a download: see https://www.gbif.org/citation-guidelines and the function occ_download() of the 'rgbif' package.

  • GBIF records are opportunistic observations. They show where the species was seen, not where it is absent, and the position can be uncertain by several kilometers.

Note

This function requires a working internet connection.

See also

get_eunis_data and get_ocsge for the land cover of the same region of interest.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
  data("roi_metaleurop")
  occ <- get_gbif_data("Apodemus sylvaticus", roi = roi_metaleurop)
  plot(sf::st_geometry(occ))

  # recent records with a position known within 100 m
  occ <- get_gbif_data("Apodemus sylvaticus", roi = roi_metaleurop,
                       year = "2000,2024",
                       coordinateUncertaintyInMeters = "0,100")
} # }
